sections.text: Compare example evaluation records before requesting a reviewUse the conditions, units and notes below to compare three fictional records. These records are provided for an offline layout exercise and do not describe any supplier or product.Request review

Example evaluation recordsRecord AlphaMeasured response93.2 %Apparent density1.25 g/cm³Specific surface area18.4 m²/gMoisture after conditioning0.18 %Observation period24 hMeasurement contextCondition A; see note 1Note 1 — Alpha was observed after dry storage at 23 °C. Its response must not be compared with a wet-conditioned result as though the methods were identical.Record Beta with an intentionally long evaluation labelMeasured response91.7 %Apparent density1.31 g/cm³Specific surface area21.6 m²/gMoisture after conditioning0.24 %Observation period48 hMeasurement contextCondition B; see note 2Note 2 — Beta was observed after humid storage at 30 °C. The surface area value belongs only to this record and does not establish performance in a finished formulation.Record GammaMeasured response94.1 %Apparent density1.19 g/cm³Specific surface area17.2 m²/gMoisture after conditioning0.15 %Observation period72 hMeasurement contextCondition C; see note 3Note 3 — Gamma was observed after sealed storage at 18 °C. The observation period describes this example measurement, not a recommended shelf life.

How to read an evaluation recordStart with the question that the record can answerA comparison becomes useful when the reader can connect each number with a specific evaluation question. Before looking for the largest or smallest value, identify what was measured, what sample was used and which conditions were applied. A result may describe one observation without answering whether another formulation will behave the same way. Read the label, unit and note as a single statement. If any part is missing, keep the interpretation open rather than treating the record as a complete recommendation. The example records above use different conditioning environments to make this distinction visible. Their numerical differences are useful for practising careful reading, but the exercise does not establish a preferred record or a purchasing decision.Keep the unit attached to the numberA number without a unit leaves the reader to reconstruct an assumption that the source should have supplied. Density, surface area, percentage and elapsed time describe different properties, even when their values happen to look similar. A narrow screen should therefore preserve the unit beside the value or repeat it in an equally clear field label. Moving a comparison into cards can make the text easier to read, provided that the card still identifies the record and every measurement. The connection must remain clear after wrapping, opening a disclosure or moving to the next card. Do not infer a unit from the previous row, and do not rely on a desktop table heading that disappears in the mobile presentation.Read conditioning notes before drawing a comparisonConditioning can change what an observation means. Temperature, moisture exposure, storage method and elapsed time are examples of context that a reader may need before treating two observations as comparable. The notes in this exercise belong to individual fictional records. They should remain close enough to their references that the reader can follow the connection without guessing. A footnote that appears somewhere else on the page is not automatically understandable. Its reference must identify which result it qualifies. If a compact layout repeats notes under each record, preserve their complete wording. If the layout uses shared notes, keep the references and navigation clear in both the initial and expanded states.Record what is known and leave room for uncertaintyAn evaluation request does not need to disguise uncertainty as a precise answer. The optional record field below allows the reader to say that a record has not yet been chosen. Context can explain the question, the intended comparison or a condition that should be considered. This information helps organise a review without claiming that a suitable result already exists. The requested quantity is a separate piece of information and uses kilograms throughout this exercise. It does not become a product recommendation or a promise of availability. When a required value is missing or invalid, the interface should explain the problem at the relevant field while retaining the information that the reader has already supplied.Distinguish preparing a request from receiving an answerPreparing a request, submitting it and receiving a substantive answer are different events. A clear interface tells the reader which event has occurred and what remains unknown. In this offline exercise, the success state demonstrates only how confirmation would appear in the layout. No message is sent, no record is approved and no review is scheduled. The wording must remain accurate even if the form looks realistic. A local simulation can show how the page behaves after a button is pressed, but it cannot prove that an external recipient accepted data. Keep this distinction visible when checking error handling, keyboard navigation and the placement of the resulting feedback.Return to the original context when revising the requestA reader may return to the comparison after starting a request. The page should support that movement without losing the connection between the record, its measurements and the question being prepared. Optional context is useful for describing a distinction that a fixed field cannot express, but it should not be used to repair a missing unit or an unclear label elsewhere on the page. Before finishing, revisit the conditioning note for the record under consideration and make sure the question still matches what the example can demonstrate. If no record has been selected, the request should preserve that uncertainty. This final check is a reading task for the exercise, not evidence of technical suitability or an invitation to infer missing facts.

const menu=document.querySelector('#menu'),dialog=document.querySelector('#menu-dialog');menu.onclick=()=>{dialog.show();menu.setAttribute('aria-expanded','true');document.querySelector('#close-menu').focus()};const close=()=>{dialog.close();menu.setAttribute('aria-expanded','false');menu.focus()};document.querySelector('#close-menu').onclick=close;dialog.addEventListener('cancel',event=>{event.preventDefault();close()});dialog.querySelectorAll('a').forEach(a=>a.onclick=close);
document.querySelector('form').onsubmit=event=>{event.preventDefault();const fields=['name','email','quantity'].map(id=>document.getElementById(id));const invalid=fields.filter(el=>!el.checkValidity());fields.forEach(el=>{const bad=invalid.includes(el);document.getElementById(el.id+'-error').hidden=!bad;el.setAttribute('aria-invalid',String(bad))});document.getElementById('form-summary').hidden=!invalid.length;document.getElementById('confirmation').hidden=!!invalid.length;if(invalid.length)document.getElementById('submit').focus()};
